Minor clarifications may be made through ordinary project communications, provided that such clarification does not materially increase the workload.
findings.explanation: Informal communication channels can easily be used by the client to request small additions that accumulate into substantial unpaid scope creep over time.
findings.suggested_change: Require all changes, clarifications, or task additions to be formally documented and approved in a written change order prior to commencing work.

findings.quoted_text: Invoices are payable Net 30. An invoice that remains unpaid after the due date may accrue interest at 1.0% per month to the extent permitted by applicable law.
findings.explanation: Net 30 terms require you to finance project deliverables for up to a month after invoicing, which can create cash flow bottlenecks for an independent contractor.
findings.suggested_change: Negotiate Net 15 payment terms and ensure upfront milestone payments are strictly enforced before work progresses.

findings.quoted_text: Either party may terminate for convenience upon 20 days' written notice, subject to payment of fees for Services properly performed through the effective termination date.
findings.explanation: A 20-day termination for convenience clause allows the client to cancel the project abruptly, paying only for work performed up to that date without covering non-cancellable expenses or lost project value.
findings.suggested_change: Extend the notice period to 30 days and add a kill fee requiring payment for all work in progress plus a percentage of remaining project fees.

content.subject: Proposed changes to the agreement
content.body: Hi, thank you for sharing the agreement. I am looking forward to collaborating, and I have a few small requests before signing. - Regarding the relevant clause on project communications, informal requests can accumulate into unpaid scope creep, so I propose that we require all changes and task additions to be documented and approved in a written change order beforehand. - Regarding the relevant clause on payment terms, Net 30 can create cash flow delays for independent contractors, so I suggest adjusting to Net 15 terms with upfront milestone payments strictly enforced. - Regarding the relevant clause on termination, a short notice period allows for abrupt cancellation without covering lost value, so I recommend extending the notice to 30 days and adding a provision for work in progress. Thank you for understanding, and I look forward to your response.
